tools.name: search_digest
tools.description: Search the public digest of HL7 standards discussions. Returns at most 20 items, each with every claim's evidence record and canonical_url — no summary text. Use get_digest_item for one item in full.

tools.name: get_digest_item
tools.description: One digest item in full: each claim (question, outcome, impact, stage, next step) with its own evidence record, plus HL7 Jira statuses and canonical_url.

tools.name: get_jira_status
tools.description: Up to 50 HL7 Jira keys: status, resolved, resolution, last_verified with its jira_verified evidence record, lifecycle stage, source_url (HL7 Jira) and the canonical_url of public items that cite it. "applied" is not "published".

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_validation_findings" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_bundle, get_validation_findings · Private data: search_digest, get_digest_item, get_jira_status · Public sink: validate_bundle, get_validation_findings, compare_igs · Destructive: get_validation_findings.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_bundle, get_validation_findings · Private data: search_digest, get_digest_item, get_jira_status · Public sink: validate_bundle, get_validation_findings, compare_igs · Destructive: get_validation_findings

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "validate_bundle" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
